lede: A detector, a tracker and fourteen explainable rules turn a fixed CCTV view into labelled events; a causal risk model watches for conflicts frame by frame.

metrics.speed_note: Observed RTX 3050 Laptop run on all four 4K originals; 3× allowed. T4 not yet verified.

learned: YOLO11 detectors pretrained on COCO: m for Part A and s for Part B on the evaluation GPU; n for CPU fallback and the demo.
A drivable-area mask learned only from where tracked vehicles move in the organiser-provided samples.
A per-cell direction field learned from sample trajectories; no hidden-test footage or hosted inference APIs are used.
rules: ByteTrack associations become smoothed trajectories with scale-normalised speed and explicit frame-edge handling.

Part A aligns hand-drawn geometry to a representative clip frame using SIFT/RANSAC. Calibrated lamps require their expected hue, including dim daylight signals; weak image matches do not inherit the camera layout.
One explainable rule per event class combines trajectories with the drawn stop line, crossings, lane directions and signal phases.
Temporal post-processing merges fragments, removes short blips, clips boundaries and guarantees no same-class overlap.
Part B is strictly causal: closest approach, braking and wrong-way evidence are fused and mapped to [0, 1]. The sigmoid parameters are heuristic; empirical calibration is still needed.

worked: Scale-normalised motion makes one threshold usable from the near foreground to the far lanes.
Ignoring boxes clipped by the image edge removed false stopped-vehicle, U-turn and collision events.
Signal-aware queue handling suppresses red-light queues when the relevant signal state is readable; unknown phases remain a limitation.
The same causal closest-approach logic runs in the submission, demo and exported risk charts.
failed: The original GPU run still contains nine unconfirmed accident candidates, including C3902 at 1.47–3.47 s. Valid output and event counts do not establish detection accuracy.
Near-miss was disabled: all 15 initial firings on synthetic clips and C3905 were false positives, mainly ordinary lane passing.
The colour-only fire/smoke heuristic is not reliable enough for hidden footage and remains disabled.
Generic static-obstacle background differencing is vulnerable to shadows and parked objects, so it remains disabled until labelled.
Unreadable or indirectly inferred traffic-signal phases can leave ordinary queues classified as stopped vehicles or congestion; these require visual review.
Small framing shifts are corrected in Part A, but continuous camera motion and severe occlusion are not handled. A new viewpoint needs its own scene geometry and learned direction field.

case_studies.title: A pedestrian beside a parked car is not a crash
case_studies.observation: The baseline GPU run proposed an accident in C3896 at 216.02–217.62 s. In this reviewed pair, the black SUV remains parked while pedestrians walk or stand beside it: a false positive from proximity and pedestrian deceleration.
case_studies.correction: The revised rule requires prior vehicle movement in a person–vehicle pair, a complete half-second settling window and observed proximity after settling. Seven regression tests cover these checks, including positive collision examples. The rule remains a heuristic, not visual proof of contact.
case_studies.scope: AI-assisted review of one pair, not an exhaustive annotation or an accuracy score. The other C3896 candidate at 274.74–276.01 s remains unconfirmed; dense traffic stopping is not enough to verify an impact.
case_studies.alt: Sixteen cropped frames show a parked black SUV with pedestrians standing and walking beside it while other cars pass in the foreground.
case_studies.caption: C3896 original · window 214–222 s · sampled at 2 fps. Frame labels are relative to the window, starting at zero. Cropping and sampling can miss brief or occluded contact. Click to inspect the full-size sheet.

next: Finish human labels for all samples and tune boundaries directly against F1 at tIoU 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7.
Train a compact accident/near-miss clip classifier on public crash datasets and use rules only to propose candidates.
Calibrate Part B on labelled pre-crash windows so the 0.5 alarm threshold has an empirical meaning.
Add operator metrics by lane and time of day, plus active-learning review for low-confidence events.
